newsitem.title: SPAIN: JP Morgan cuts Spanish Equity Market weighting.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan cuts Spanish Equity Market weighting.

text.p: JP Morgan Securities Ltd said on Thursday it was downgrading the Spanish Equity Market to neutral from overweight.

"We are downgrading our recommended weighting in the Spanish equity market from overweight to neutral. Central to this view is our belief that there is more limited upside to earnings forecasts in the Spanish equity market than for many other European equity markets," it said in a research note.
The bottoming of inflation could prompt a more modest market performance medium-term, while short-term rates are likely to be on hold near-term, disappointing the market, the note said.

JP Morgan said it expects the Bank of Spain to cut rates by 75 basis points following the September presentation of the 1998 budget plan, with the Bundesbank increasing rates by 150 basis points to bring about convergence.
Specifically, JP Morgan suggested selective profit-taking in banks.

"We would recommend selective profit-taking among Spanish banks as a way of playing a consolidation in the overall market...The domestic banks look particularly vulnerable to falling short-term interest rates," the note said.
It also said Repsol and Telefonica had gone through target prices.
